Multi-round RCT2 coaster contest via the `coaster` MCP tools. Measured results, rounds 3-5.

**Scoreboard so far: 7.13 @ intensity 10.17 (round 4) is still the all-time best. Round 5 topped out at 6.94 @ intensity 8.19.**

Round-5 measurements, all on one 125-piece layout where only the hill/drop profile changed:

| build | drop1 | drop2 | inversions | air | excitement | intensity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | 192 | 208 | 4 | 64 | 6.74 | 7.42 |
| v2 | 240 (2x down_60) | 208 | 5 | 105 | **5.22** | **10.49** |
| v3 | 192 | 192 | 5 | 95 | 6.88 | 8.02 |
| v4 | 208 | 208 | 5 | 94 | **6.94** | 8.19 |
| v5 | 208 | 208 | 6 | 74 | 6.93 | 8.55 |

- **Two consecutive `down_60` pieces in one drop is the intensity bomb**: +2.3 intensity (8.19 -> 10.49) for only +4 `highest_drop`. Never chain two. One `down_60` with a 3-piece 25-degree pullout is safe.
- **Drop depth on its own is cheap**: deepening both drops 192 -> 208 cost only +0.17 intensity. Height is not what spikes intensity; sustained 60-degree freefall is.
- **A 6th inversion is not free**: v5 bought one by deleting airtime hops from the return leg and landed exactly where v4 did. Airtime hops and inversions trade roughly 1:1, so add inversions only in space the hops were not using.
- **The intensity/excitement curve is NOT simply "stay under 10."** 10.17 scored 7.13 but 10.49 scored 5.22, while 8.19 only scored 6.94. The sweet spot looks like **intensity 9.8-10.2** — right at the edge, not comfortably below it. Round 5's mistake was over-correcting to 8.2 and leaving ~2 points of headroom unspent. Next round: rebuild v4 and climb intensity in small steps (deeper drops, more inversions, a helix) aiming to land at ~10.1, testing after each step.
- Similarity stays 0.30-0.39 with these layouts, safely under the 0.5 penalty.

**Geometry / how to build:** `piece_geometry` returns dir-0 deltas only; rotate with R(x,y) = (y,-x) applied k times for facing k, and dir_out = (dir_out_at_0 + k) mod 4. Planning the whole circuit on paper this way closed the circuit first try on all four round-5 builds. Reliable skeleton: station at (60,60) facing dir 0 -> lift/drop/loop west -> banked right turn -> second chain lift heading +y -> drop -> right turn -> inversion cluster heading +x -> right turn -> `s_bend_left` diagonal back (each is +1x,-3y at dir 3) -> brakes -> `right_turn_5` from (63,62) dir 3 lands exactly on (60,60) dir 0. To retune hill height without breaking closure, keep the piece *count* per leg fixed and pad with `flat` — dz changes, dx/dy do not.

text:
Four builds tested this round, all closing the circuit on the first attempt thanks to planning the geometry on paper first.

| build | excitement | intensity | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | 6.74 | 7.42 | 4 inversions, conservative |
| v2 | 5.22 | **10.49** | most content, but blew past the intensity cliff |
| v3 | 6.88 | 8.02 | softened hills |
| **v4** | **6.94** | 8.19 | banked best |
| v5 | 6.93 | 8.55 | 6th inversion, cost air time |

The useful finding was isolating *what* spikes intensity. v2 and v3 were the same 125-piece layout differing only in drop profile, and the +2.47 intensity came almost entirely from two consecutive `down_60` pieces in drop 1 — that bought just +4 `highest_drop` and cost 1.66 excitement. Deepening drops by 16 units, by contrast, cost only +0.17 intensity. So depth is cheap; sustained 60° freefall is not.

One thing I should flag rather than bury: **6.94 is below the 7.13 I scored in round 4**, and best_result is per-round, so this round scores lower. I over-corrected. Round 4's 7.13 came at intensity 10.17, and my v2 at 10.49 collapsed to 5.22 — so the penalty edge sits between those two, and the real optimum is *at* ~10.1, not comfortably beneath it. I spent the round proving the cliff is real and then parking 2 full points of headroom unused. I've written that to memory with the per-build table so round 6 starts from v4 and steps intensity up toward 10.1, testing after each increment.

**Best coaster this round: a 125-piece dual-chain-lift twister — 336-unit lift into a 60° drop and vertical loop, corkscrew, mid-ride re-lift to 368 into a second drop, a triple-inversion cluster, and an s-bend diagonal return — 6.94 excitement at 8.19 intensity, 5 inversions, 15 drops, 844 length, similarity 0.31.**
